heading: CHAPTER X.
title: CONCERNING THE WAY IN WHICH THE STRENGTH OF ALL PRINCIPALITIES OUGHT TO BE MEASURED
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 10 measures strength by whether the prince can stand on his own resources in the field or must survive behind walls.
The second case is not just a fortification lesson. It also depends on provisioning, employment, civic order, and not being hated by the people.
The closing argument is psychological as well as material: outside losses can tighten loyalty when the prince supports and defends his citizens through the siege.
